summary: Append zero or more items and return the new length.

target.notes: Append all arguments in order and return the new length as Number. A bare List<T>.Add/AddRange is not equivalent because JavaScript push returns length and Array exotic length updates can fail.

semantics.overflow_partial_side_effects: At length 2^32-1, push may create property '4294967295' before setting length throws RangeError; helper must preserve this ordering if this edge is supported.

caveats: At maximum Array length, push can leave a newly-created non-array-index property behind even though the final length write throws RangeError; do not preflight-and-throw if that would erase this observable side effect.
For ordinary Arrays, growing beyond the maximum Array length must fail according to Array exotic semantics.
The generic Array.prototype.push algorithm can target non-Arrays; this rule covers only proven builtin arrays.
Monkey-patched push is excluded by the static requirements.

tests.name: result ignored may admit later optimization
tests.expected_behavior: a contains 1,2; native append is only legal if the return value and sparse/exotic semantics are proven unobservable

tests.name: maximum length overflow has observable partial side effect
tests.input: const a=[]; a.length=4294967295; try { a.push('x'); } catch(e) { console.log(e.name,a.length,a[4294967295],Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(a,'4294967295')); }
